To tune the component controls, shakedown tests were conducted to ensure stable operation of the HP-TES for the six operating modes listed: • Cooling HP operation (no TES) • Cooling HP-TES discharge • Cooling HP-TES charge • Heating HP operation (no TES) • Heating HP-TES discharge • Heating HP-TES charge The control objective is to maintain the subcooling of the outdoor EXV (or brazed PHX EXV for discharge modes) by controlling the opening degree of the corresponding EXV. Figure 55 shows the LabVIEW interface of the DAQ system during the heating discharge mode shake-down test. Figure 55: LabView interface of the DAQ system (left) and PID control (right) Table 13 shows the relay control signals for the actuators in different operating modes, implemented in the LabVIEW-based DAQ station. The functions have been tested successfully. Figure 56 shows the overall terminals for the lab tests. A check valve was installed between the reversing valve RV2 and the accumulator to prevent backward flow in heating discharge mode when the outdoor temperature is low. Moreover, due to differences in internal volume among the three heat exchangers, in specific modes (e.g., heating discharge mode), the outdoor EXV should remain open to control the amount of refrigerant circulating in the system. To achieve the appropriate opening of the outdoor EXV and ensure the proper level of VCC system subcooling, PID controllers have been implemented in LabVIEW, with subcooling set to 5 K.
